headline: Grand Theft Auto 2 gets path tracing and 60 FPS frame generation via RTX Remix
summary: A new mod harnesses Nvidia's RTX Remix technology to add full path tracing and dynamic time-of-day cycles to the 27-year-old classic, Grand Theft Auto 2.
details: Modder gebdag has unveiled GTA2 RTX Remix, a mod that harnesses Nvidia’s RTX Remix technology to add full path tracing and dynamic time-of-day cycles to the 27-year-old classic, Grand Theft Auto 2. The mod requires a custom Direct3D 9 renderer to bridge the gap between the original game's legacy APIs and RTX Remix.

The mod dramatically overhauls the game's visuals, adding realistic lighting and shadow effects, dynamic day-night cycles, and improved reflections for elements like explosions and neon signs. Players can also tweak lighting settings via an in-game menu.

Beyond the graphical enhancements, GTA2 RTX Remix supports widescreen 16:9 displays, offers frame rates up to 60 FPS through Frame Generation technology, and fixes issues with cars and pedestrians popping in at screen edges.

The project is open-source and available on GitHub. To use it, players need a copy of Grand Theft Auto 2 (tested with version 9.6), a 64-bit version of Windows 10 or 11, and the required RTX Remix runtime files.
Grand Theft Auto 2 joins other classic games like Need For Speed Carbon, Tomb Raider, Max Payne, and The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind that have received similar graphical overhauls using RTX Remix.
